The state is proportional to \((1+i)|\uparrow\rangle + (2-i)|\downarrow\rangle\). Its normalization constant is \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{|1+i|^2 + |2-i|^2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2+5}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\). So the normalized state is
\[
|\alpha\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\big[(1+i)|\uparrow\rangle + (2-i)|\downarrow\rangle\big].
\]

The operator \(A\) has matrix elements \(A_{ij} = \hbar/2\) for \(i \neq j\) and \(0\) otherwise. In the \(\{|\uparrow\rangle, |\downarrow\rangle\}\) basis,
\[
A = \frac{\hbar}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_x.
\]
The eigenstates of \(A\) are those of \(\sigma_x\):
\[
|+\rangle_x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|\uparrow\rangle + |\downarrow\rangle), \quad |-\rangle_x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|\uparrow\rangle - |\downarrow\rangle),
\]
with eigenvalues \(+\hbar/2\) and \(-\hbar/2\).

The probability of measuring \(+\hbar/2\) is \(|\langle+_x|\alpha\rangle|^2\):
\[
\langle+_x|\alpha\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\big[(1+i) + (2-i)\big] = \frac{3}{\sqrt{14}} \quad\Rightarrow\quad P(+) = \frac{9}{14} \approx 0.64.
\]
The probability of measuring \(-\hbar/2\) is \(|\langle-_x|\alpha\rangle|^2\):
\[
\langle-_x|\alpha\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\big[(1+i) - (2-i)\big] = \frac{-1+2i}{\sqrt{14}} \quad\Rightarrow\quad P(-) = \frac{1+4}{14} = \frac{5}{14} \approx 0.36.
\]

The expectation value of \(A\) is
\[
\langle A \rangle = \left(+\frac{\hbar}{2}\right)P(+) + \left(-\frac{\hbar}{2}\right)P(-) = \frac{\hbar}{2}\left(\frac{9}{14} - \frac{5}{14}\right) = \frac{\hbar}{2}\cdot\frac{4}{14} = \frac{\hbar}{7}.
\]

These match option (B).

Answer: B
